summary: The 2026 Iran war (the US and Israel against Iran, since Feb 28) has heated up again after a tense pause: over Nov 15-16 Iran's forces claimed several tankers hit mines in and near the Strait of Hormuz, UKMTO reported a tanker hit by a projectile, and Euronews reported US strikes on Iranian missile launchers at Bandar Lengeh and Sirik. Iran says the strait stays shut to unapproved shipping, the US now has three carriers in the region, and Iranian state-aligned media reported Iran's foreign minister met Oman's foreign minister in Muscat on Nov 17 to discuss Hormuz shipping, with no agreement reported. Brent fell nearly 2% on Monday to below US$94 on surplus expectations.

status.label: Strait of Hormuz
status.note: Iran says it is closed to ships that don't coordinate with its Persian Gulf Strait Authority; the US says the main routes are controlled by the US and its regional partners. Most traffic moves through a shuttle system the US coordinates with Arab partners, with weekly volumes swinging as attacks continue (Al Jazeera).

status.label: Oil through Hormuz
status.note: About 11.6 million barrels a day over the seven days to Oct 13, about 68% of the 17.1 million pre-war baseline (Kpler, via Al Jazeera).

status.label: The war
status.note: US officials said the US carried out limited, defensive strikes on Iranian targets, including on Qeshm Island near the Strait of Hormuz on Nov 2, after Iranian surface-to-air missile threats; they said it was not a resumption of major combat (Wall Street Journal, then Reuters). Indirect talks through Qatari mediators continue with no breakthrough announced; Vice President Vance said there has been progress. On Nov 7 the US carried out further strikes on Iranian air defences on Qeshm Island, which President Trump called minor (Euronews). On Nov 8 Trump told CNN renewed attacks were highly unlikely if talks make real progress; no deal has been signed.

status.label: Brent crude
status.note: Brent fell nearly 2% on Monday, Nov 16, to below US$94 a barrel as the IEA pointed to a fourth-quarter surplus and Chinese demand weakened, despite fresh tanker attacks (Trading Economics; CNBC on surplus expectations).

updates.text: Tehran Times reported that Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi met Oman's foreign minister in Muscat on Nov 17 to discuss shipping arrangements in the Strait of Hormuz; no agreement was reported.

Euronews reported that the US struck Iranian missile launchers in Bandar Lengeh and Sirik on Sunday night, after Iranian missiles targeted tankers and drones hit Bahrain's Al Riffa base; CENTCOM denied damage to US assets.

UKMTO said an oil tanker was hit by an unidentified projectile early Monday, causing an engine-room fire; no casualties were reported. The USS Theodore Roosevelt arrived, giving the US three carriers in the region.
sources: gCaptain: UKMTO reports two tanker attacks

updates.text: Iran's army navy said a fourth tanker hit a mine east of the Strait of Hormuz; the claim was not independently verified.
Iran's navy said an oil tanker caught fire after hitting a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz (reported by ANI and Mehr News; not independently verified).
sources: ANI: Oil tanker catches fire after hitting naval mine in Hormuz, says Iranian Navy
Mehr News: Oil tanker burns after mine strike in Strait of Hormuz
Al Arabiya: Oil tanker on fire in Strait of Hormuz due to naval mine, Iran's army says

updates.text: President Trump said the US no longer needs a deal with Iran, Trading Economics reported as oil trading reopened.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards warned ships that the Strait of Hormuz is closed, after claiming a six-drone attack on a US radar at Bahrain's Al-Riffa base; Bahrain said the drones were intercepted.
A G7 statement shared by the US Embassy in Riyadh condemned Iran's attacks on its neighbours, Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and Iran's disruption of shipping through Hormuz.

background: The war began on Feb 28, 2026 with US and Israeli strikes on Iran. An April ceasefire collapsed on July 8. The US has blockaded Iranian ports since April (reinstated in July); Iran restricts and attacks shipping through Hormuz, which carried about a fifth of the world's oil before the war.
factcheck: Checked by Claude against at least two reputable sources where possible. Statements by Iran's military, the US military (CENTCOM) or President Trump are labelled as claims, because each side's account of who controls the strait differs.
